atoms.text: Jamie has made a list of some things she wants to do. She can do some of them straight away, while other things will take time and effort to achieve.

trainers.instruction: Sort Jamie’s wants into those she can fulfil now and those she can achieve later.

atoms.b: buy sweets with her pocket money

feedback.wrong: If Jamie wants to, she can just go to the shop and buy some sweets right now. She doesn’t need to take other steps before.

atoms.b: get a B on her next maths test

feedback.wrong: To achieve this, Jamie has to take extra steps such as practising for the test. She cannot do this right away.
Jamie can immediately take out her pencils and start drawing.
To accomplish this, Jamie will need some time as she has to read one book after another.
While Jamie might have to wait for her favourite show to come on, she doesn’t need to take extra steps to be able to do this.

atoms.b: learn to play a song on guitar

feedback.wrong: Although Jamie might be able to start practising right away, it will take her some time to memorise the song.

trainers.instruction: Take a look at Jamie’s list and fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: The activities listed under “Now” don’t need a lot of ((++planning interest)) or many different ((++steps people)) to complete them. They are quick and ((++easy difficult)) to achieve.
atoms.sound: The activities listed under now, don’t need a lot of planning or many different steps to complete them. They are quick and easy to achieve.

atoms.b: The activities listed under “Later” are ((easier ++more_difficult)) to achieve. They need extra resources, such as time or skills, that ((++aren’t are)) available right now. We can also call these “Later” activities goals.
atoms.sound: The activities listed under later, are more difficult to achieve. They need extra resources, such as time or skills, that aren’t available right now. We can also call these “Later” activities goals.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct statement.

b.sound: A goal is something you work towards to achieve in the future.
A goal is something you work towards to achieve in the past.
Goals are only small things, like brushing your teeth in the morning.
Goals can be big or small. For example, to learn a new skill or to save money.
To reach a goal, you don’t need to plan at all.
To reach a goal, you need to think about the steps you will take.
You  need to take action to complete a goal.
You can complete a goal by forgetting about it.

feedback.end: By taking action, you can influence whether you reach your goal or not.

trainers.instruction: Can your actions influence whether this happens?
